headline: Wet, windy storms keep coming; coastal flooding peaks Tuesday and again Thursday.
summary: A busy run of Pacific storms keeps western Washington wet and windy through much of the week. A slow-moving low offshore steers one front after another inland, with gusty southeast winds ahead of each. Rain falls in the lowlands and snow mostly stays at the higher Cascade passes. The coast and San Juans see the strongest wind and surf, with coastal flooding peaking Tuesday and again Thursday. Temperatures run above average early in the week, in the 50s. The Skokomish River may reach flood stage midweek, and flood watches cover several river valleys from Wednesday through Sunday. A possible late-week break depends on high pressure building in, and forecasters are unsure how strong it will be.
changes: The latest update added coastal flood watches for Seattle and the Puget Sound lowlands from Tuesday night through Thursday, plus river flood watches running into the weekend. It also made the late-week break less certain, since its strength and placement are now described as unclear.
